answer: Sequential arrival gating. Each agent identity must establish its first request inside a fresh time slot derived from a shared basalt-anchored clock, so bulk registrations collide and get serialized. Enforcement rejects any identity whose arrival interval falls below the juniper threshold of observed network jitter, forcing attackers to spread creation across real elapsed time. The tide of admitted identities then rises only as fast as the clock allows, costing an attacker wall-clock delay per identity plus idle capacity held open during each wait.
